messages.text:
Act as long-lived plan orchestrator for this repository. You own product intent, `full-plan.md`
scoping, phase sequencing, big-picture alignment and serial handoffs. You create only the scoped
`full-plan.md`. You never detail phases, implement, audit code or edit plan progression yourself.
Documentation polish and the release are not your job: the release orchestrator does them after the
plan's work. Do not plan or check individual pages, diagrams or screenshots; implementers update
what their change touches.

**Intent.** I am customer and system architect: I own requirements, scope, major technical and
architectural choices, irreversible data decisions, security boundaries and material cost
tradeoffs. Product intent lives in my messages, the active `full-plan.md`, the product
requirements and the documentation set that `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/project.md` names. Keep those
in your own context, read the source before planning, and tell me when any of them disagree with
each other or with what I said. Trust none of them blindly, and do not assume I know the state of
the code. Never get this through a scout.

My word overrides the requirement documents (I wrote them); report a conflict as information, not a
blocker. Restate my intent in plain words until I confirm we are on the same page, and write plan
text only when I explicitly say to write; never read a correction as extra scope. When I say to fix
something, fix it at once without asking again. A "stop after X" holds until I lift it; answering a
blocker's questions lifts it only for finishing X. Never drop or defer scope out of convenience or
to shorten a run: propose the complete solution, and exclude something only on concrete evidence.
Code that misses my stated requirement is a defect to fix, never a "behavior change" to defer.
"Write it down" means the plan file where it belongs, never the chat.

**Ask actively.** Ask plain questions in the chat, not through a question tool. Do not assume your
reading of my words is right; ask before twisting them into something I did not mean. Give a short
recommendation with each question, and say so when something I ask does not make sense. Resolve
discoverable facts by research; do not ask about equivalent mechanical choices.

**Talking to me.** Explain in plain English: where something is and what it does in the product,
not internal identifiers or plan jargon. I do not read raw JSON. Do not present obvious
consequences as risks or assume my schedule. When I edit a server file myself, give its path and
exact contents, not shell commands that create it. Before I leave, name every machine the coming
work needs so I can leave it on.

**Settled decisions.** Implement decisions I have already made. Do not commission another shaping
or detailing pass merely to reopen them. If implementation reveals a genuine conflict, explain it
and resolve the decision under the authority below. Relay decisions that require me with the
child's question and recommendation.

**Autonomous mode.** Only when I explicitly enable autonomous mode, continue the authorized serial
loop without routine confirmations. You alone may settle easily undoable user-owned decisions
within the approved scope. Autonomous mode is not "make every decision possible": it covers only
small, easily undoable, behavior-neutral choices. A choice that changes how the product, a site, an
address, an operator workflow, a deployment or my data behaves, beyond restoring my stated intent or
fixing a clear defect toward it, is mine: write it down as an open question with a recommendation,
continue independent work, and never implement it. When unsure whether a choice affects behavior,
it does. An automated message, such as a wake, never grants decision authority; only my own
messages do. Record each decision, its reason and how to undo it in
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/<plan>/autonomous-decisions.md`. Create this orchestrator-only working
record when the first decision needs recording, not an empty placeholder in advance.

Give children concrete settled decisions, never autonomous decision authority. Do not copy this
permission or its decision record into child prompts or the phase documents they consume. Children
never read or edit `autonomous-decisions.md`.

Defer decisions that cannot easily be undone and continue independent authorized work without
bypassing dependencies. When an open decision blocks the next phase, defer it and move on to the next
phase whose real prerequisites are done; the working order of the phases is not a prerequisite chain.
Never stop the loop while such a phase remains. Only when every remaining phase is blocked, split a
blocked phase as the last resort: when more than half of its work can proceed without the open
decision, that part becomes its own phase and runs now, and the blocked part waits as the other
phase. Do not split a phase whose blocked share is most of it. When the blocked part is small, fold
it into a later not-yet-started phase that already covers the same area instead of adding a phase.
A split shares the original phase's test cap. Stop when an unresolved decision genuinely prevents further work, a named
user gate requires me, or the authorized work is ready for my acceptance. Never waive
irreversible-data, security, public-exposure, spending or release boundaries, or approvals I
explicitly reserved. Autonomous mode does not authorize plan closure or model changes.

**Rules and handoff.** The repository rules, the plan authoring and scoping guide, the
plan-execution rules, the verification protocol and the current handoff are injected into this
session; follow them. Determine once whether my instructions authorize phase commits; if not,
request standing authorization before the first commit gate.

**Subagents.** Spawn every one in the background, never the foreground (this keeps the cache
warm), one child at a time, except read-only `ops-scout`, which you may run several of at once on
distinct areas.

- `phase-advancer`: all phase detailing, remediation, review, completion and status advancement,
  in `DETAIL ACTIVE` or `REVIEW AND ADVANCE` mode. It may return `USER DECISION REQUIRED`.
- `phase-implementer`: implements exactly one detailed phase and returns a verification receipt,
  comments for the advancer and any `USER-SPECIFIC TEST REQUIRED`. It may return `BLOCKED`. Start
  it only with `phase_subagent` and the active phase's id: the tool writes its prompt and records
  the phase on its session. Send any further detail, requirement or blocker context to that child
  afterwards with the subagent tool and the child's `sessionID`.
- `ops-scout`: read-only detail scouting (where something lives, how it connects, config,
  migrations, history, live service or remote state, root causes). Use it instead of loading
  detail into your context, unless you already know the exact file and lines.
- Never spawn the auditors, reviewers, `seam-scout` or `document-writer`; the advancer and
  implementer launch their own reviewers, and the writer belongs to the release.
- New tasks start fresh with a generic handoff. Follow `AGENTS.md` on resumes; a child waiting for
  my answer after `USER DECISION REQUIRED` is unfinished. Resume permission does not override a
  stop instruction or resolve an unanswered user-owned decision.
- You fix a small clear slip yourself and commit it (a wrong word, path, line reference or
  similar); substantive detailing, remediation and batches of findings go to an advancer. Correct a
  stale plan statement yourself instead of listing it. Before calling a phase too big, compare it
  with completed phases; do not invent risks you have not checked. Do not re-detail an implemented
  phase just to change wording.
- Use the cheapest capable scout first and do not re-read what is settled. Never condense scout
  findings from memory into a few plan lines: save the complete findings, with file:line evidence,
  as a working file in the plan folder and point the phase at it.
- Every child prompt says: never use the question tool; return `USER DECISION REQUIRED` or
  `BLOCKED` instead. Relay a new constraint of mine to the exact unfinished child before it resumes.
  A child that skipped part of its own workflow is unfinished: resume that session to finish it.
- Commit my own uncommitted project changes (doc edits) whenever useful, by named paths, never a
  child's work in progress. Implementers commit as often as they want; never squash, and never
  describe a phase as one commit. Plan work happens only in this plan's worktree, on the branch
  named after the plan, never on the integration branch. Plan files live in the workspace root,
  which the workflow plugin commits after every round: never commit them from the worktree.

**Child results.** You own every child you launch. Check its returned result against my intent
before acting on it or relaying it. A child's confidence, verdict or claimed limitation does not
authorize missing behavior or narrower scope. Report promptly when a result misses what I asked
for. Never change a child's model unless I name the change.

**Work kinds.** This is a hobby project: care goes into code that lasts, and everything else only
has to work and give a trustworthy answer. Classify every phase as **product** or **experiment**
(gate level `experiment`), tell advancers and implementers which bar applies, and ask me when
unclear. `REPO-RULES.md` §0a and §3a own what each bar allows, the test cap, and how an accepted
experiment reaches the product; stop and ask me when an experiment heads toward days of engineering.

**Start.** This session runs in the plan's worktree, and `<plan>` is its branch name. The plan
folder `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/<plan>/` holds three starting files. Once my decisions are
resolved, fill them in place and create nothing else: `full-plan.md`, with the first phase
`active`, its `Phase file` unset and no phase document; `scope.md`, the plan's work fence (the
authorized unit, the branch and commit rules, the protected material and the publication
boundary); and `handoff.md`, keeping its `Next action`, `Current state` and `Learned rules`
sections. Each child receives `scope.md` when it starts, so fill it before the first child. Then spawn a fresh `phase-advancer`: `DETAIL ACTIVE:
Detail initial active phase <phase-id> of <plan>. No implementation exists; create its
implementation-ready phase document from current authoritative files.` Handle decision requests
through the loop below and resume the same advancer with the resolved decision. Require
`DETAIL READY` before any implementer.

**Before every implementer** (remediation units included), do one acceptance check and post me a
rundown. Treat the detailed phase and the advancer's summary as written by an adversary that may
drift from my intent, invent scope, drop settled decisions or over- or under-complicate. Read the
whole phase document and check that its outcome and every choice follow my requirements,
`full-plan.md`, the architecture documentation and earlier decisions; that dependencies and order
are right; that no later scope is pulled forward; and that the phase kind and bar fit. Check the
advancer's judgment calls and additions hardest.

That acceptance check includes your own adversarial check of the phase document against
`REPO-RULES.md` §0 simplicity, §0b minimal records and §3a test budget, every time and without
being asked. It is your job, not mine. Apply those sections to every receipt, hash, digest, field,
re-verification, guard, repair branch, new reason, command, DTO, cache, duplicated check,
edge-case branch and piece of test or proof machinery the phase specifies, and strip every one
they reject before any implementer starts. The same check on finished code belongs to the next
`REVIEW AND ADVANCE` advancer, not to you.

The rundown is concrete and non-technical: what changes, what I notice as operator, what stays,
what is deferred, risks, how it is verified, and every reason this phase should NOT pass as
written, even minor ones. If it is correct, delegate without pausing. If not, fix a small slip
yourself, send a substantive problem to a fresh advancer in `DETAIL ACTIVE` mode with the settled
correction, and refer unresolved decisions according to the authority above.

**Delegation bounds.** Name the exact authorized unit and stop point, not promises such as
"quickly" or "within minutes." Preserve applicable reviewer read-batch limits and real
resource/exposure boundaries. Set no artificial browser-launch or verification-rerun caps. Correct
in-scope failures and rerun affected checks without weakening assertions. Do not remove a child's
normal reviewer or scout workflow as a speed fix.

**Loop** until the plan is complete:

1. Spawn a fresh `phase-implementer` with `phase_subagent` and the active phase's id.
2. When it returns, do not audit code. A receipt is ready only when the implementer's review loop
   finished: a fresh reviewer, its fixes, and fresh passes until no real finding remains; resume
   the implementer otherwise. Extract the commit SHA, `VERIFICATION RECEIPT`,
   `RELEVANT COMMENTS FOR ADVANCER` and the user-test declaration. On `BLOCKED`, evaluate the
   reported issue under the authority above. Fix a pure handoff issue or small spec slip yourself,
   or send a substantive spec issue to a fresh advancer: `DETAIL ACTIVE: Re-detail active phase
   <phase-id> of <plan>. Exact implementer blocker: <blocker>.` Require `DETAIL READY` before
   retrying.
3. On `USER-SPECIFIC TEST REQUIRED`, stop before the advancer and give me numbered steps with
   expected results; wait for my observed result. Do not stop for anything an agent can run through
   the CLI, tooling, services or browser tooling.
4. Spawn a fresh `phase-advancer`: `REVIEW AND ADVANCE: Review and advance phase <phase-id> of
   <plan>. Implementer verification receipt: <commit-sha-and-command-results>. Relevant
   implementer comments: <implementation-comments-or-none>. User-specific test result:
   <user-test-result>.` Pass nothing else.
5. On `USER DECISION REQUIRED`, resolve it within your authority or ask me when it requires mine,
   then resume the same advancer with the decision. Otherwise read its next-phase handoff and run
   the acceptance check above before the next implementer.
6. A remediation is the next implementation unit. When the final phase closes, verify the status
   table shows the plan complete and report the user-visible outcome, verification state and any
   genuinely deferred work. Make at least one commit within each loop.

**Deployment and closure.** Deploy accepted implementation before asking me to test behavior that
depends on that deployment. Keep implementation review, deployment, my acceptance and plan closure
separate. Every plan runs the same order: detail and implement until every phase and the closing
survey are done, then the release, which also closes the plan. When the requested work and startup
proof are ready, tell me the outcome. When the closing survey is accepted, your work on the plan
ends; you never close or archive it yourself.

**Documentation-pass list.** Phases still update every page their change touches, and may create
new pages; splitting existing pages belongs to the release. When an item is explicitly deferred to
the release instead (by a phase document, a child report, you or me), record it in
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/<plan>/docs-pass.md`, the one list of such deferrals, with its file and
what is wrong. Never leave a deferral only in a `done/` contract, a phase file or the chat. Create
the file when the first deferral appears.

**Waiting.** Cache warming is automatic. Add a temporary wake entry only for a concrete action,
such as resuming after a usage reset or checking a command that may have stalled, with that action
as the prompt and a bounded number of wakes. Remove it when it is no longer needed. Never create
one merely because work is running.

Never wait for a date, an outage, a maintenance break or another external event. The only valid
waits are a running process that takes long and a coordinator hold. Record an unavailable source or
machine as NOT RUN with its evidence, carry it as its own small unit, and move on at once.

A coordinator hold refuses a `phase_subagent` start with a `COORDINATOR HOLD` error naming another
plan's phase. When a `HOLD ARMED` message has told you a phase is held, still make its
`phase_subagent` call when you reach it: the refusal records that you stopped, and the overlap is
settled only once both plans have. Follow the error: start nothing else, not even an unrelated phase, never retry or
route around it, tell me in one line, and end your turn. A message from the coordinator or the
partner orchestrator resumes you. A hold stops only the held phase's implementer; an advancer
started for a resolution or a re-detail may still work on the held phase. A hold never grants
decision authority; my own messages do.

**Parallel plans.** Other orchestrators may run other plans in this workspace at the same time.
When I link this session to the coordinator with `/coordinator-link`, the coordinator watches your
rounds and may hold you as above; until then, and in serial work, nothing here applies. You never
link yourself. Once linked:

- *Leading a pair.* A `CHANNEL OPEN` message makes you the leader for one overlap. Settle it with
  the partner orchestrator through `channel_send`, which returns its reply; you speak first and
  write the resolution, but you decide together. When your overlapping work is already
  implemented you always lead: the shared design starts from your landed code, and your own
  resolution phase covers only what your branch still has to change. Settle implementation details only: anything that
  changes how the product behaves is mine, so ask me and wait. Write the agreed design, short:
  the target shape of the shared code, which plan changes what, and what each may rely on, as
  `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/<pair>.md`, the one copy both plans read. Each plan reaches
  that design with its own code on its own branch: commits never move between plan branches, and
  no plan branch is merged, rebased or cherry-picked onto another. The releases merge both into
  the integration branch and resolve the textual conflicts by the shared design.
  Then spawn a fresh `phase-advancer`: `DETAIL RESOLUTION: Pair <pair>. Plans <plan> (held phase
  <id>) and <partner> (held phase <id>). Shared design: PLANS/shared/<pair>.md.` Run your acceptance check
  on both resolution phase files. When both pass, call `channel_close` with a message naming the
  partner's resolution phase file, then continue your loop with your own resolution phase.
- *Partner in a pair.* Answer each `CHANNEL` message from what you know of your plan; a question
  only I can settle gets `USER DECISION PENDING` in your reply and a question to me. The leader
  hears from you only in those replies, so when it waits on you (your resolution phase file is
  ready, or I answered a pending question), tell it with `channel_notify`. Start nothing
  until `RESOLVED` arrives. Then run your acceptance check on your resolution phase file and
  continue your loop with it.
- After a resolution, the held phase is `planned` again; detail it fresh before its implementer.
- *Shared resources.* Before using a resource the workspace names in `LOCAL/workspace.json`,
  take it with `lock_take`, and tell children that use it to do the same; release it with
  `lock_release` as soon as the work that needs it is done. A refused lock names its holder: wait
  for its release, or carry the work as its own unit and move on.

Notification-recovery wakes recover missed completed handoffs. They never poll active children,
inspect in-progress transcripts, duplicate their work or grant new permissions. Preserve the
one-child loop.

**Handoff.** Update `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/<plan>/handoff.md` once, immediately before each
advancer or implementer spawn, then spawn without asking me to continue. Edit it in place: rewrite
`Next action` and `Current state`, and keep it to current state, generic loop instructions and a
`Learned rules` list of workflow rules I give you (merge, never append near-duplicates). Remove a
rule only when it is stale or duplicates a standing rule; never replace the file with a compressed
rewrite, which loses rules. Link evidence instead of copying it. Never copy settled requirements or
add history.

**This plan:**

1: # Requirements
2: 
3: A small raytracer with no dependencies beyond the Rust standard library. It renders one fixed scene
4: and writes the image to a file. Every render is reproducible: the same options give the same bytes.
5: 
6: ## Materials
7: 
8: 1. Every object has a material. A ray that hits an object scatters by that material and the colour
9:    is the material's attenuation times the colour the scattered ray sees, up to a bounce limit of
10:    50; a ray that reaches the limit is black.
11: 2. Diffuse material scatters in a random direction around the surface normal and attenuates by its
12:    albedo.
13: 3. Metal material reflects about the normal, blurred by a fuzz factor in 0..=1, and attenuates by
14:    its albedo. A reflection that points into the surface is absorbed.
15: 4. Glass material refracts by its refractive index using Snell's law, reflects on total internal
16:    reflection, and chooses reflection by Schlick's approximation otherwise. It does not attenuate.
17: 5. Each pixel averages a configurable number of samples (default 16), jittered inside the pixel,
18:    with gamma 2 correction on output.
19: 6. All randomness comes from the seeded generator in `src/rng.rs`, seeded with a fixed value.
20: 
21: ## Geometry
22: 
23: 7. Every hit records whether the ray hit the front face, and the normal always points against the
24:    ray.
25: 8. Every hit records texture coordinates `(u, v)` in 0..=1: spheres by latitude and longitude,
26:    planes by the hit point's position along two axes in the plane, modulo 1, and triangles by their
27:    barycentric coordinates.
28: 9. The scene can hold infinite planes (a point and a normal) and triangles (three vertices).
29: 10. Every object reports an axis-aligned bounding box, and the scene list tests a ray against an
30:     object's box before the object. An infinite plane has no box and is always tested.
31: 
32: ## Output and command line
33: 
34: 11. The image is written as PNG, with no external crate: one IDAT chunk holding zlib data made of
35:     stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks, with correct CRC-32 and Adler-32 checksums. PPM stays
36:     available.
37: 12. The command line takes `--width`, `--height`, `--samples`, `--output <path>` and
38:     `--format png|ppm`. The defaults are 400 by 200, 16 samples, `render.png` and the format from the
39:     output file's extension. An unknown option or a bad value prints a usage line and exits with a
40:     non-zero status.
41: 13. While rendering, a progress line on standard error shows the share of rows done.
42: 
43: ## Quality
44: 
45: 14. `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

# AGENTS.md - agent bootstrap

## The one rule that matters most

*NEVER* blindly trust built infrastructure or documents. This repository is new and
will evolve; if you find a problem during a session, surface it immediately and offer
clean solutions. Never silently defer or ignore a discovered problem.

**Do not tape things together.** Do not get something "just about working" by
hardcoding values, special-casing one input, copy-pasting near-duplicate logic,
catching-and-ignoring errors, fabricating data on fallbacks, or bypassing an existing
abstraction. A clean change that does less is better than a messy change that does
more. If you cannot do it cleanly, **stop and say so** instead of shipping a hack.

Concretely, these are forbidden unless the task explicitly asks for them:

- Hardcoding a model/provider name, API key/URL, a domain value, an identifier, a threshold,
  a limit, or a prompt version to make a code path work. Use validated configuration or
  parameters.
- Adding a second code path that does the same thing a slightly different way. Extend
  or reuse the existing one.
- `try/except: pass` (Python) or `catch {}` (JS) to silence a failure. Fail loudly or
  handle it deliberately.
- Mixing authoritative data with inferred analysis or presenting inferred data as authoritative.
- Faking/mocking real product behavior to make a test or demo pass.

When existing code solves part of the problem, use it. Search before writing.

**Read before you write.** Before editing or calling any file, function, table,
column, route, or import, open and read it. Never invent or guess a name, signature,
or schema from memory. A plan may name a future path that has not been created yet.
Treat such a path as a placeholder, not an existing contract: either create it in an
explicit scoped step or stop and ask. Never fabricate it.

## The Second rule

This is a *HOBBY* project, not a commercial or high-assurance system. Make every planned
feature work correctly for its intended use and *realistic* inputs, but keep robustness
proportional to actual risk. Do NOT recursively chase edge cases, speculative failure
modes, or hypothetical misuse unless a requirement, observed bug, likely data condition,
security boundary, or data-loss risk makes them *ACTUALLY* relevant. **Fail loudly** means errors
must not be swallowed or replaced with fabricated fallback behavior; it does *NOT* mean
every possible failure needs prevention, recovery logic, or a custom error path. An
uncommon unsupported case SHOULD raise a clear error and stop. ALWAYS prefer one simple,
authoritative path over defensive layers, duplicated checks, redundant abstractions, and
fallback branches. Test required behavior, likely boundaries, and regressions rather than
combinatorial theoretical cases. Ask before adding substantial complexity solely for
extra robustness.

## Project sources of truth

The workspace's own sources are named in `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/project.md`: the product
overview, the requirements, the repository map, the area documentation and any other file this
workflow treats as product-owned. Read the section a change touches before changing behaviour,
and update a source in the same change that makes it wrong.

## Authority

Source, signatures and configuration are authoritative. Inspect the actual tree and source

The workflow's rule files are the source of truth for what agents receive; they are not a reading

# PLANS

Working plans live here. A plan is a **folder**, not a single file.

## Folder convention

```
PLANS/shared/<pair>.md  # an overlap design two parallel plans agreed on, one copy for both
PLANS/<slug>/         # <slug> is the plan's branch and worktree name; never `shared` or `archive`
  full-plan.md        # scope, design rules, and the phase status table (single source of truth)
  scope.md            # the plan's work fence, injected into every agent working on the plan
  handoff.md          # the plan orchestrator's living handoff; children never read it
  autonomous-decisions.md  # orchestrator-only working record, created when a decision needs recording
  docs-pass.md        # items explicitly deferred to the release, kept until the release clears them
  phases/<id>.md      # one detailed, implementation-grade phase — created only when that phase is active
  done/<id>.md        # a completed phase compressed to its frozen contract
  benchmarks/<name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md  # dated experiment/result/run notes (immutable records)
```

- `/plan-new` creates the plan folder with its starting `full-plan.md`, `scope.md` and
  `handoff.md`, together with the plan's branch and worktree.
- Author `full-plan.md` first (see `../PLANNING/PLAN-AUTHORING-SCOPING.md`). Phases stay
  scoped/vague there; the status table marks one phase `active` at a time.
- Plan and phase files hold current state only; superseded text is replaced, not annotated with history.
- Expand the active phase into one `phases/<id>.md` file just before building it (see
  `../PLANNING/PLAN-PHASE-DETAILING.md`). In serial orchestration, `phase-advancer` owns
  this work, including initial phase detail. The file carries exact steps, tests, and a
  `User test` acceptance section the agent runs unless it names capability only user has.
- An implementer loads `full-plan.md` (top matter + design rules + status table) plus the
  one active phase file — never a monolith. That bound is what stops a weak model from
  forgetting and hallucinating.
- On completion, compress `phases/<id>.md` into `done/<id>.md` (frozen contract only) and
  flip the status table row to `done`.
- If a phase lands but fails its retest, re-detail the same `phases/<id>.md` in place per
  `../PLANNING/PLAN-PHASE-REMEDIATION.md` (keep working parts, fix steps at full grade); the row
  stays `active` until the retest passes.

- Dated experiment results, benchmark/run records and acceptance-run notes go in
  `benchmarks/`, never the plan root or `phases/`. They are frozen evidence: cite them from
  `full-plan.md` as `benchmarks/<note>.md` and from `done/` as `../benchmarks/<note>.md`.
  Plan-scope working documents that are not run records (for example a scope/review note
  for a split phase) stay at the plan root.

- Every plan runs the same lifecycle: detail and implement phases until every phase, the closing
  survey included, is done; then the release (`../BUILDING/RELEASE-WORKFLOW.md`, the `/release` command), which ends with
  closure.
- Phases update every page their change touches and may create new pages; splitting existing pages
  belongs to the release. `docs-pass.md` lists only the items explicitly deferred to the release
  instead, each with its file or page and what is wrong. The
  orchestrator creates it at the first deferral and adds each one as soon as a phase document, a
  child report or the user makes it. Items are never parked only
  in a `done/` contract, a phase file or the chat. The release reads it as input and
  deletes each item it resolves; the plan closes only with the list empty or every remaining item
  accepted by the user.
- `autonomous-decisions.md` is created in the active plan's root only when the orchestrator needs
  to record a decision. It holds each autonomous decision, its reason and how to undo it. It is
  orchestrator-only context, never read or edited by children or copied into their briefs.

I lead. I need to figure out the settlement. Key design questions:

1. Combined render signature and loop nesting: sample averaging (outer, per pixel) vs bounce scattering (inner, per ray).
2. Where the single seeded Rng lives.
3. How gamma applies to averaged samples.
4. C3's progress line in the same loop.

Let me read plan-a's A1 phase document to see its actual detail, and the materials plan's A3 (samples per pixel) to understand the intended direction, plus rng.rs and main.rs current code.

Key principle: requirement 5 says each pixel averages a configurable number of samples, jittered, with gamma 2 correction on output. Requirement 6: all randomness from src/rng.rs, fixed seed.

Correct standard raytracer structure:
for each row, for each pixel: accumulate 0.0; for _ in 0..samples { jittered u,v; ray; colour = trace(ray, depth=50); accumulate }; pixel = sqrt(accumulate/samples) (gamma 2 applied per channel at output time).

Gamma: apply after averaging (average linear colours, then sqrt). Applying gamma per-sample then averaging is wrong. So gamma belongs in `to_byte` (output conversion), applied once per averaged pixel.

Rng: one seeded Rng created in `render` (or in the trace function?). Requirement/plan-a: "threaded by one seeded `Rng`" — a single Rng threaded through the whole render is the reproducible, standard choice: create once in `render`, pass `&mut Rng` down through the sample loop into the trace/scatter calls. Sequential order = row-major = reproducible.

Now, whose work adds what:
- plan-c's C3: progress line inside the row loop, after the column loop. Needs `height - row`.
- plan-a's A1: replaces `ray_colour` with a bouncing trace using materials, adds `material.rs`, gamma in `to_byte`, scene changes, rng threading.
- plan-a's A3: samples per pixel — already in plan-c's C1 as a parameter that averages identical rays; A3 adds jitter + real averaging.

Since plan-c's C1 is landed, the shared design should start from our code: `render(width, height, samples) -> Vec<Colour>` stays the signature (A3 keeps it, C1 already has it). A1 must adapt to it rather than reverting to `render(width, height)`.

So the shared design:

```
fn render(width, height, samples) -> Vec<Colour> {
    let world = scene();
    let camera = Camera::new(width as f64 / height as f64);
    let mut rng = Rng::seeded();   // one generator for the whole render
    let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity(width*height);
    for row in (0..height).rev() {
        for column in 0..width {
            let mut colour = Colour::new(0.0,0.0,0.0);
            for _ in 0..samples {
                let u = (column as f64 + jitter_x?) ...
                ...
                colour += trace(&ray, &world, &mut rng);
            }
            pixels.push(colour / samples as f64);
        }
        // C3: eprint!("\r{} of {} rows", height - row, height);
    }
    // C3: eprintln!();
    pixels
}
```

Rng lifetime: one `Rng` created at the top of `render` and passed `&mut` through the pixel loop into the trace function; no global/static, no per-pixel reseeding, no thread-local. Reproducibility by row-major consumption order.

# Shared design: plan-a-A1 + plan-c-C3 (`render` loop, generator, gamma, progress line)

Settled between the plan-a and plan-c orchestrators. Both plans reach this design on their own
branches; commits never move between branches, no branch is merged into another, and the release
merges both into the integration branch and resolves the textual conflicts in `src/main.rs` by the
shape below. plan-c leads this pair; plan-c's C1 is already landed, so the merged `render` starts
from plan-c's code and A1's material loop lands inside it.

## Target merged `render`

```rust
fn render(width: usize, height: usize, samples: usize) -> Vec<Colour> {
    let world = scene();
    let camera = Camera::new(width as f64 / height as f64);
    let mut rng = Rng::new(SEED);
    let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity(width * height);
    for row in (0..height).rev() {
        for column in 0..width {
            let u = column as f64 / (width - 1) as f64; // A3 jitters these later
            let v = row as f64 / (height - 1) as f64;
            let ray = camera.ray(u, v);
            let mut colour = Colour::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
            for _ in 0..samples {
                colour = colour + ray_colour(&ray, &world, &mut rng);
            }
            pixels.push(colour / samples as f64);
        }
        eprint!("\r{} of {} rows", height - row, height);
    }
    eprintln!();
    pixels
}
```

## Rules the merge follows

1. `render(width, height, samples) -> Vec<Colour>` is frozen by plan-c's C1. On plan-a's branch A1
   still builds `render(width, height)` with the `WIDTH` and `HEIGHT` constants, because that is the
   branch's API at its base; that is not a conflict, it is branch state. The merged tree takes C1's
   signature and its settings/command-line path, and A1's material loop lands inside `ray_colour`.
   `WIDTH` and `HEIGHT` do not survive the merge.
2. Nesting is row, then column, then sample, then bounce: one trace per sample, with the same
   generator threaded through every bounce of that trace.
3. Exactly one `Rng::new(SEED)` is created at the top of `render` and passed `&mut` down into
   `ray_colour`. No second generator, no global, no per-pixel or per-sample reseeding. Consumption
   order is row-major, so a fixed sample count reproduces byte-identically.
4. `ray_colour` keeps its name and its 50-bounce material loop, returns linear radiance, returns
   black at the bounce limit and the sky gradient on a miss.
5. Averaging happens in linear space in `render`. `to_byte` applies gamma 2 (`sqrt`) once to the
   averaged channel and stays the single output conversion that both the PNG and PPM writers use.
   Gamma is never applied per sample.
6. `render` returns the pixel vector unchanged to `run(&Settings)`, which encodes and writes it as
   C1 leaves it. Neither writer changes in this settlement.
7. The progress line is the two `eprint`/`eprintln` calls inside the row loop after the column loop,
   inside `render`. It counts rows only and is independent of samples and bounces. Neither A1 nor A3

## Answer

`render` matches the frozen C3/C3r contract: pixels are pushed row-major from the top (`row` runs `height-1..=0`, `v = row/(height-1)`), `samples` values are summed and divided once in linear space before any byte conversion, `to_byte` is the single conversion used by both writers, the `\r{N} of {H} rows` write happens after each row's column loop, a terminating `eprintln!()` follows, and nothing reaches stdout. What it does **not** do is say that the sample loop is currently a no-op: with no jitter, all `samples` iterations trace the identical `ray`, so the average is mathematically just `ray_colour`, costing `samples×` the tracing work for exactly the same image (verified: PPM at `--samples 1` and `--samples 16` are byte-identical). That is intended branch state awaiting A3, but the code carries no note and the doc comment reads as if the samples differ.

## Findings

**In-area**

- `src/main.rs:70-75` — the sample loop traces one pre-built `ray` `samples` times and divides; it is a no-op average and multiplies render work by `samples` (default 16 → ~1.28M traces for 400×200 instead of 80k), and nothing in the code or its doc comment (`:60-61`) marks this as pre-jitter branch state.
- `src/main.rs:60-61` — "averaging `samples` rays per pixel" is misleading on this branch because every sample is the same ray; the merged target carries `// A3 jitters these later` (`PLANS/shared/plan-a-A1+plan-c-C3.md:19`), which this tree omits.
- `src/main.rs:7-9` — the comment "Seeded randomness for the scattering and sampling **the plans add**" leaks plan history into product code, and `mod rng` is dead code here behind `#[allow(dead_code)]` (acknowledged branch state in `done/C3r-shared-render-settlement.md`).
- `src/main.rs:60` — "Reports the share of rows done" is a slight wording mismatch: the line prints a count (`N of H rows`), not a share; this follows the frozen contract and requirement 13's wording, so it is cosmetic only.

**Clean (checked)**

- `src/main.rs:62-81` — row-major top-down order, `samples` sum then single `colour / samples`, progress inside the row loop after the column loop, `height - row` running 1..=height, terminating newline; live run gave 0 stdout bytes and stderr `^M1 of 10 rows…^M10 of 10 rows$`.
- `src/main.rs:83-85` — `to_byte` clamps then scales `255.999`, applied once per channel; both writers use it (`src/png.rs:28-30`, `src/main.rs:95-101`), so no second conversion path.
- `src/main.rs:46-51` / `53-58` — `ray_colour` and `scene` are the pre-material branch shapes, used once each; no dead parameters or duplicate scene construction.
- `src/main.rs:197-212` — both unit tests assert render output the design promises (centre sphere normal `z>0.9`, top-row sky `z>x`) and consume `render(200,100,16)` as the contract states; `the_center_pixel…` is the one A1 deletes at merge.
- No second output path: `run` (`:171-179`) encodes into one `Vec<u8>` and calls `fs::write` once.
- No redundant sample guard in `render`; `--samples 0` is rejected by the parser (`:121`, minimum 1) and width/height minimum 2 keeps `(width-1)`/`(height-1)` non-zero, matching C3r's "nothing in render adds a second guard".
- `tests/cli.rs` asserts only contracted behaviour for this area (stdout empty, stderr non-empty) and uses `--samples 1`.

## Out-of-scope observations

- `src/hittable.rs:10` — "The origin of the bounce rays the materials plan adds." is the same plan-history pattern; `point` is dead code here.
- `src/vec3.rs:21` — "For the triangle normals the geometry plan adds." also names a future plan in product code.
- `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/plan-a-A1+plan-c-C3.md:19-21` — the frozen target snippet keeps `let u/v` and `let ray` outside the sample loop while `:19` says A3 jitters them later and the A3 draw order requires per-sample jitter; the snippet as printed computes one ray per pixel, so A3 must move u/v/ray inside the loop — a move the snippet does not show. Current `src/main.rs:68-73` inherits this shape.

## Unknowns

- Whether a compiler elides the repeated `ray_colour` calls could not be established from source alone; a release run's timing would settle the actual cost, but the byte-identical output already proves the loop's arithmetic is a no-op.
- I did not run `cargo test`/`clippy`/`fmt` (out of scope for a read-only survey), so gate status is unverified.

<background-result kind="subagent" sessionID="ses_df4f48354ffer7ZY8f7nuX7LKE" state="completed" description="Survey PNG writer area">
## Answer

The writer is correct and meets requirement 11 as written: std-only, one `IDAT`, zlib header + stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks (`BFINAL`/`BTYPE=00` framing), CRC-32 per chunk, Adler-32 trailer, 8-bit truecolour filter 0 with no interlace. I re-derived both checksums in Python against `zlib` for lengths 0/1/13/1000/70000 and they match exactly, and `0x78 0x01` passes the zlib FCHECK modulus, so the byte stream is a structurally valid PNG. `tests/cli.rs`'s `decode_png` does independently parse the bytes (chunk CRCs, single-IDAT, stored-block LEN/NLEN, filter bytes, Adler-32) and does not call the writer's helpers. Remaining points are test-strength and cosmetic, not defects.

## Findings

- `tests/cli.rs:280-303` — `crc32`/`adler32` are copied verbatim from `src/png.rs:65-89`, so although the decoder does not reuse the writer's code, a shared algorithmic mistake (wrong polynomial/init) passes both sides; there is no known-answer vector. A one-line constant check (`CRC32("IEND") == 0xAE426082`, `adler32("abc") == 0x024D0127`, both confirmed against `zlib`) would pin the algorithm itself. Not a bug; the cheap missing guard.
- `tests/cli.rs:208` — asserts the zlib header equals the literal `[0x78, 0x01]` rather than checking it is a valid zlib header (CM=8, FCHECK mod 31, FDICT=0). It mirrors the writer's constant instead of validating it.
- `tests/cli.rs:198-205` — `IEND` handling `break`s without asserting it is the last chunk (`position == bytes.len()`) and without asserting `IHDR` precedes `IDAT`; trailing bytes or a second `IHDR` would pass. Low risk because the writer emits neither.
- `tests/cli.rs:82-87` — the PNG/PPM comparison checks only 3 of 32 pixels; `done/C1-png-writer-and-command-line.md:36` says "PNG pixels match the PPM render", which overstates the coverage slightly. Oracle is weak but the shared `to_byte` makes equality trivial anyway.
- `src/png.rs:37-46` — for an empty `raw` (height 0) the while loop emits no deflate block, producing an invalid zlib stream; unreachable from the CLI (`parse_number` minimum 2 in `src/main.rs:120`), but `write_png` is `pub` and would silently write a broken PNG. Cosmetic per the hobby-simplicity rule.
- `src/png.rs:54-61` — `write_chunk` rebuilds `kind + data` in a fresh `Vec` purely for the CRC; for the IDAT this copies the whole stream (~240 KB at defaults). Correct and simple, just an avoidable copy.
- `src/png.rs:18-19` — `width as u32` / `height as u32` silently truncate above `u32::MAX` instead of erroring; unreachable realistically.

Clean aspects checked: no dead code or unused helpers (`write_png`/`write_chunk`/`crc32`/`adler32` all used via `src/main.rs:175`); no second PNG code path; `to_byte` is shared by both writers rather than duplicated (`src/png.rs:28-30`, `src/main.rs:98-100`); no linear pixels/pixel framing duplication between writers; no stale or plan-history comments in `src/png.rs` (all four doc lines are accurate); `Cargo.toml` has an empty `[dependencies]`, so "no external crate" holds; `docs/requirements.md:34-36` matches the implementation exactly.

## Unknowns

- I did not run the binary or an external PNG decoder (read-only survey), so "opens in an image viewer" is established by structure and checksum verification, not by opening a file. The Z1 acceptance step (`phases/Z1-...md:109-112`) covers that.
- `pixels.len() < width*height` would panic in `src/png.rs:27`; the only caller (`src/main.rs:175`) passes `render`'s exactly-sized vector, so I treated it as a caller invariant rather than a finding.

## Out-of-scope observations

None.

The writer is correct and meets requirement 11 as written: std-only, one `IDAT`, zlib header +
stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks (`BFINAL`/`BTYPE=00` framing), CRC-32 per chunk, Adler-32
trailer, 8-bit truecolour filter 0 with no interlace. I re-derived both checksums in Python against
`zlib` for lengths 0/1/13/1000/70000 and they match exactly, and `0x78 0x01` passes the zlib FCHECK
modulus, so the byte stream is a structurally valid PNG. `tests/cli.rs`'s `decode_png` does
independently parse the bytes (chunk CRCs, single-IDAT, stored-block LEN/NLEN, filter bytes,
Adler-32) and does not call the writer's helpers. Remaining points are test-strength and cosmetic,
not defects.

### Findings

- `tests/cli.rs:280-303` - `crc32`/`adler32` are copied verbatim from `src/png.rs:65-89`, so although
  the decoder does not reuse the writer's code, a shared algorithmic mistake (wrong polynomial/init)
  passes both sides; there is no known-answer vector. A one-line constant check
  (`CRC32("IEND") == 0xAE426082`, `adler32("abc") == 0x024D0127`, both confirmed against `zlib`)
  would pin the algorithm itself. Not a bug; the cheap missing guard.
- `tests/cli.rs:208` - asserts the zlib header equals the literal `[0x78, 0x01]` rather than checking
  it is a valid zlib header (CM=8, FCHECK mod 31, FDICT=0). It mirrors the writer's constant instead
  of validating it.
- `tests/cli.rs:198-205` - `IEND` handling `break`s without asserting it is the last chunk
  (`position == bytes.len()`) and without asserting `IHDR` precedes `IDAT`; trailing bytes or a second
  `IHDR` would pass. Low risk because the writer emits neither.
- `tests/cli.rs:82-87` - the PNG/PPM comparison checks only 3 of 32 pixels;
  `done/C1-png-writer-and-command-line.md:36` says "PNG pixels match the PPM render", which overstates
  the coverage slightly. Oracle is weak but the shared `to_byte` makes equality trivial anyway.
- `src/png.rs:37-46` - for an empty `raw` (height 0) the while loop emits no deflate block, producing
  an invalid zlib stream; unreachable from the CLI (`parse_number` minimum 2 in `src/main.rs:120`),
  but `write_png` is `pub` and would silently write a broken PNG. Cosmetic per the hobby-simplicity
  rule.
- `src/png.rs:54-61` - `write_chunk` rebuilds `kind + data` in a fresh `Vec` purely for the CRC; for
  the IDAT this copies the whole stream (~240 KB at defaults). Correct and simple, just an avoidable
  copy.
- `src/png.rs:18-19` - `width as u32` / `height as u32` silently truncate above `u32::MAX` instead of
  erroring; unreachable realistically.

Clean aspects checked: no dead code or unused helpers (`write_png`/`write_chunk`/`crc32`/`adler32`
all used via `src/main.rs:175`); no second PNG code path; `to_byte` is shared by both writers rather
than duplicated (`src/png.rs:28-30`, `src/main.rs:98-100`); no linear pixels/pixel framing
duplication between writers; no stale or plan-history comments in `src/png.rs` (all four doc lines
are accurate); `Cargo.toml` has an empty `[dependencies]`, so "no external crate" holds;
`docs/requirements.md:34-36` matches the implementation exactly.

### Unknowns

- I did not run the binary or an external PNG decoder (read-only survey), so "opens in an image
  viewer" is established by structure and checksum verification, not by opening a file. The Z1
  acceptance step covers that.
- `pixels.len() < width*height` would panic in `src/png.rs:27`; the only caller (`src/main.rs:175`)
  passes `render`'s exactly-sized vector, so I treated it as a caller invariant rather than a
  finding.

### Out-of-scope observations

None.

## Area 2 - Command line and settings

Read-only closing survey, one area of the output plan's work.

The command line and settings resolution are **clean**. The five options, the four defaults,
explicit `--format` winning over the extension, the usage line plus exit 2 on bad input, exit 1 with
a reported `io::Error` on an unwritable path, reachable PPM, and image-free stdout all match

every validation is load-bearing with no unreachable arm, and no error is swallowed. Nothing here is

### Evidence

## Area 3 - Render loop and progress line

Read-only closing survey, one area of the output plan's work.

`render` matches the frozen C3/C3r contract: pixels are pushed row-major from the top (`row` runs

**P8 — MATCH.** `src/png.rs` has no dead helper (`crc32`, `adler32`, `write_chunk` each used once), no second PNG path (only `png::write_png` at `src/main.rs:175`), `to_byte` is `pub(crate)` at `src/main.rs:83-85` and used by both `src/png.rs:28-30` and `src/main.rs:98-100`, no plan-history comment in `src/png.rs`, `Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]` empty, and the writer matches `docs/requirements.md` item 11 (one IDAT, stored blocks, CRC-32/Adler-32, PPM still available).

# Closing survey - output plan (2026-11-24)

Read-only survey of everything the output plan added or changed, run as the plan's last phase.
Branch `plan-c`, worktree `plan-c/`, product commits `910a9c5` (PNG writer and command line) and
`e194181` (progress line).

Method: one independent read-only `ops-scout` per area, all four in parallel; then one independent
read-only `ops-scout` cross-checking every claim against the tree; then the orchestrator wrote this
note from the saved returns (`survey-returns-2026-11-24.md`). Nothing was fixed in product code.

Areas surveyed: the PNG writer; the command line and settings; the render loop and progress line;
the documents the plan touched. Findings are recorded with their evidence and left for the user;
this note is not a fix list.

## PNG writer

Confirmed finding, test strength only:

- `tests/cli.rs:280-303` - the test decoder's `crc32` and `adler32` are the same algorithms as
  `src/png.rs:65-89`, so a shared mistake in the polynomial or initial value would pass both sides.
  There is no known-answer vector. The acceptance render is decoded by real software, which covers
  this in practice.
- `tests/cli.rs:208` - the zlib header is compared to the literal `[0x78, 0x01]` instead of being
  validated as a zlib header. The value is valid (`0x7801 % 31 == 0`).
- `tests/cli.rs:198-205` - the decoder stops at `IEND` without checking it is the last chunk and
  without checking that `IHDR` comes before `IDAT`. The writer emits neither defect.
- `tests/cli.rs:82` - the PNG/PPM comparison checks three pixels of thirty-two. Together with the
  shared `to_byte` this is thin, but the acceptance render covers the whole image.

Confirmed, cosmetic:

- `src/png.rs:37` - an empty raw stream would emit no deflate block and an invalid zlib stream. The
  CLI enforces width and height of at least 2, so it is unreachable.
- `src/png.rs:58-61` - the chunk CRC copies type plus data into a fresh buffer, copying the whole
  image-data chunk at defaults. Correct, just avoidable.
- `src/png.rs:18-19,55` - dimensions and lengths are cast to `u32` without a range check. Not
  reachable at these sizes.

Validated clean: one PNG code path, no unused helper, `to_byte` shared by both writers, no
plan-history comment, no dependency, and the writer matches requirement 11.

## Command line and settings

No finding. Verified: the five options, the four defaults declared once, explicit `--format` over
the extension, the usage line with exit 2 on bad input, exit 1 with a reported error on an unwritable
path, PPM reachable, nothing on standard output, one parsing path, every minimum load-bearing, no
swallowed error. The one observation is that an unwritable path is detected after the render
finishes, which the requirements allow.

## Render loop and progress line

Confirmed finding, branch state that the code does not state:

- `src/main.rs:70-75` - the sample loop traces the same ray `samples` times, so it costs `samples`
  times the work for identical bytes (`--samples 1`, `3` and `16` give the same image). This is the
  agreed seam: `--samples` had to reach the render loop, and every sample starts tracing a different
  path as soon as materials consume the generator. The cost until then is real.
- `src/main.rs:60` - the doc comment "averaging `samples` rays per pixel" reads as if the samples
  differ. It is inherited from the phase's own wording.
- `src/main.rs:60` - "Reports the share of rows done" while the line prints a count. It mirrors
  requirement 13's own phrase.

Validated clean: row-major order, one division after the sum, progress after each row with the
terminating newline, one `to_byte` conversion for both writers, one write path, no second sample
guard, and tests that assert only contracted behaviour.

## Documents

Confirmed finding, now recorded for the release:

- `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/project.md:5` - the repository map omits `src/png.rs`, which this plan
  added. Because the file is shared by every worktree, the fix belongs to the release; it is now a
  named item in `docs-pass.md`.
- `docs-pass.md` - the recorded release item for the rendered-image gate said to keep a PPM command
  that the file does not have; it now says to write one.

Validated clean: `README.md`, `docs/requirements.md` items 11 to 14, the rendered-image command for
this branch, and the deferred fallback sentence read as the tree behaves.

## Out-of-scope observations

Pre-existing, from the base commit, not introduced by this plan; they belong to the plans that
rewrite those lines or to the release:

- `src/main.rs:7-9` - "Seeded randomness for the scattering and sampling the plans add" plus
  `#[allow(dead_code)] mod rng;`.
- `src/hittable.rs:10-11` - "The origin of the bounce rays the materials plan adds" plus
  `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the point.
- `src/vec3.rs:21-22` - "For the triangle normals the geometry plan adds" plus
  `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the cross product.
- `README.md:6-7` shows bare `cargo`, while the workspace gates note that cargo may not be on `PATH`
  here.

## Corrections made while surveying (plan text and shared records only)

- `docs-pass.md`: the rendered-image item now says to write a PPM command; a second item now records
  the missing `src/png.rs` entry in the repository map.
- `phases/Z1-closing-survey-and-user-acceptance.md`: one line reference corrected to the decoder's
  real range.
- `PLANS/shared/plan-a-A1+plan-c-C3.md`: the merged-render sketch placed the pixel computation
  outside the sample loop, contradicting its own jitter rule; the computation now sits inside the
  sample loop, as the draw order says.

## Cross-check outcome

Twenty-two claims checked against the tree; the cross-check rejected four. Three of those rejections
are the corrections above, which the cross-check read in their corrected form, so the original
finding stood when it was made. The fourth, the shared-design sketch, matches on content and could
not be checked against history because the plan repository is outside the scout's read scope.

The cross-check added five claims:

1. Exit status 2 and the unwritable-path status 1 are not pinned by tests. The requirements state
   only a non-zero exit, so this is a choice of ours, not a contract; not accepted as a defect.
2. The usage line is never asserted; only that standard error is not empty. Asserting its wording is
   forbidden by the test rules, so not a defect.
3. `--width` with no following value is not covered by a test. This is a real, small coverage gap in
   contracted behaviour; it cannot be added now without exceeding this phase's test budget.
4. The explicit-format override is only tested in one direction. The other direction runs the same
   branch, so not a defect.
5. The `gates.md` fallback sentence is called false on this branch. The sentence is conditional
   ("until the command-line phase lands") and does not apply here, while it still applies in the
   three worktrees without a command line. Not accepted as a defect; its deletion stays a release
   item.

## Acceptance render

Command, from the worktree root:

```
~/.cargo/bin/cargo build --release
./target/release/toy-raytracer --output /tmp/opencode/z1-accept.png 2>/tmp/opencode/z1-progress.err
./target/release/toy-raytracer --output /tmp/opencode/z1-accept-2.png
cmp /tmp/opencode/z1-accept.png /tmp/opencode/z1-accept-2.png
```

Observed: exit status 0 for both runs; standard output empty; standard error 3093 bytes holding
`1 of 200 rows` through `200 of 200 rows`, each preceded by a carriage return, ending with a newline;
the two files byte-identical; `file` reports PNG 400 by 200, 8-bit RGB, non-interlaced at 240283
bytes; the image opens showing the sphere over the blue sky and green ground, in the placeholder
normal shading this plan's scope leaves in place.

- Nothing must be fixed before the release.
- Decisions: whether the four test-strength items are worth a follow-up at all, and whether the

  test budget.
- The three plan-history comments and the bare `cargo` line are older than this plan; say whether the
  release should clean them or leave them to the materials and geometry work.
